ui_accessibility_analysis.problem: The tooltip is incorrectly associated with the 'Back' icon. This will provide incorrect information to the user and is a fundamental accessibility failure. Users relying on screen readers will not receive the intended 'Back' action information, or will receive incorrect information.
ui_accessibility_analysis.explanation: Changing the `data-tip` attribute to `data-title` is the correct way to define a tooltip for accessibility. `data-title` is a standard HTML attribute that screen readers correctly interpret.

ui_accessibility_analysis.problem: The absence of an appropriate ARIA role and label for the dynamically generated card list creates a serious accessibility issue. Screen readers cannot determine that this represents an interactive list of options. This is a critical failure.
ui_accessibility_analysis.explanation: Adding `role="list"` and a wrapper `<div>` around `cardList` will inform screen readers that this is a list of interactive elements. The additional `{{cardList}}` ensures the content is read out.

ui_accessibility_analysis.problem: The use of the `text-red-600` class is visually only and provides no accessibility information to assistive technology users. It provides no alternative text for the user.
ui_accessibility_analysis.explanation: Adding `aria-label="No exam form available"` provides screen readers with an accessible label for this message.

ui_accessibility_analysis.problem: The dynamic rendering of the `selectedProgram?.fullProgramTerm` creates a poor user experience, particularly for screen reader users. The text is not read out correctly for users who rely on screen readers.
ui_accessibility_analysis.explanation: Adding a space after the ellipsis in the rendered text improves readability for screen readers. This prevents the program term from being read as an incomplete phrase.

ai_analysis.problem: The Vue3Lottie component can be vulnerable to XSS attacks. User supplied content within the animation data could be used to execute arbitrary JavaScript code.
ai_analysis.explanation: This implementation uses `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` to allow the JSON to be rendered in the component. This is an extremely dangerous operation and should be avoided unless absolutely necessary.  Only use if you are 100% certain about the source and contents of the JSON.

Span elements are for inline content; `font-medium` should be applied to a heading or other semantically appropriate element.  This affects screen reader users as the heading information is not correctly announced.
ui_accessibility_analysis.explanation: Changing the `span` to an `h1` element provides the heading information to screen readers, ensuring a better user experience. Also, the new heading tag is more semantic.
